test: K562 chromatin state predicting per-gene responsiveness to perturbation
log: LOOP 245 -- CHROMATIN STATE AND WHICH GENES MOVE AT ALL
The graph explains ~0.05 of a knockdown's response (loops 242-243). The quantity
that keeps carrying signal is not which perturbation was applied but which genes
move at all. That is what chromatin is asked here.
Every mark is K562, matched to the Perturb-seq line. The 20 replication-timing
files on disk were NOT used: an ENCODE query per accession showed none is K562
(erythroid progenitor, CyT49, hepatocyte, myoblast ...). A cross-cell-type feature
dressed as a K562 feature would be loop 240's defect in a new costume.
Perturb-seq: 11,258 screened perturbations x 8,175 genes
responsiveness = sd of each gene's change across all 11,258 perturbations

T7 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
Responsiveness is a variance. A gene with low expression has few counts and its
variance is dominated by sampling noise, so any feature correlated with expression
predicts it partly for a measurement reason. T3 bounds this; it does not remove it.
Peak calls are binary summaries of a continuous signal: a gene just below a calling
threshold scores identically to a gene with no mark at all.
One cell line. Chromatin is the most cell-type-specific data in this project, so
nothing here transfers to A549 or RPE1 without being re-measured.
The marks and the Perturb-seq come from different laboratories and K562 stocks.
